correctness.rationale: The common-age tensor-product density, normalized coherent overlaps, exponential difference law, and absolutely convergent Bessel expansion yield exact purity. An independent Fock-basis evaluation verifies normalization. Strict monotonicity follows termwise from positive I_k. Fixed-rate Bessel asymptotics admit a summable dominating sequence; all crossover endpoints have explicit rigorous bounds or dominated convergence, including rates depending on N. 120 independent finite numerical checks passed; none are relied on as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Reviewed four highly relevant accessible primary papers, including the full originating boson study and a general quantum-reset spectral theorem, and compared what their statements mathematically imply rather than merely comparing titles. The evaluated all-n purity, fixed-rate coefficient and full sqrt(N) reset-rate crossover were not stated or evaluated in inspected material; basic regeneration and coherent overlaps are explicitly prior. Exact priority among all possible phase-diffusion theorems is not independently settled.
residual_risks: Broad Gaussian coherent phase-diffusion or oscillator decoherence formulas may be equivalent under a Fourier/Laplace transformation and imply pieces of the finite-n result.

A general unindexed theorem for sharp purity crossover of coherent phase mixtures could subsume the asymptotic profile; searches and accessible primary inspection do not establish absolute world-wide novelty.
The physical product-state label interpretation does not establish mode entanglement or genuinely quantum entanglement from a positive Rényi entropy combination.

value.rationale: The exact N-dependence and sharp dimensionless reset-rate threshold resolve the meaningful physical question of how fast one must reinitialize an increasingly large quantum-reset ensemble to prevent extensive loss of purity. The nontrivial universal erfc crossover, strict rate trichotomy, and fixed-rate logarithmic entropy growth express a qualitative control regime not reducible to a single finite calculation; separability clarifies its interpretive boundary.
